messages:
maria: heads-up, we just started seeing sustained 95-99% GPU memory on dedicated-eu-central and queue depth spiking. autoscaler suppressed due to quota. fallback to hosted enabled automatically. :rotating_light:
capacity-bot: [ALERT] pool=dedicated-eu-central mem_util=97.8% gpu_pods=214/220 queued_reqs=432 overflow_policy=hosted_fallback at 2026-03-18T15:20:34Z
sam: confirmed, i'm seeing a bunch of 503s in the gateway logs for routes pinned to the dedicated pool. could be an unexpected workload spike from internal batch jobs.
liam: @sam any quick way to identify which customers or jobtypes started the spike? can we throttle non-prod?
sam: yes — tailing the ingress: `kubectl logs -f gateway-5b7 -n prod | grep 503 | head` shows many requests from svc-ingest-batch. also large token counts on some requests.
anjali: i'm looking at deployment audit — there was a canary from datapipe-team rolled out 2m ago, annotated `priority=low` but routed to dedicated due to default routing.
nora: any customer-facing impact? do we need to page CS?
maria: so far error spike is internal + a few low-tier webhooks timed out. no enterprise SLAs hit yet. throttling non-prod should reduce a chunk.
liam: i'm going to adjust routing weights to divert ~30% of traffic to hosted while we triage. running: `rictl route update --pool-weight dedicated-eu-central=70 --pool-weight hosted-eu=30 --dry-run=false`
deploy-bot: ran `rictl route update` by liam (change-id: ch_8fb2). new weights applied.
capacity-bot: [INFO] fallback traffic applied. observed 28% of traffic now hitting hosted-eu. hosted queue length up but healthy.
sam: gateway 503s dropping ~60% after reroute, but tail latency on hosted is +40ms. acceptable for now.
anjali: can we throttle the datapipe batch? who owns it? @datapipe-team? (cc @maria)
maria: pinged datapipe slack, they acknowledged. asking to pause non-essential jobs.
liam: also kicking an emergency scale: `infractl pool scale --pool dedicated-eu-central --delta +12 --reason "emergency spill response"`
capacity-bot: scale request accepted, provisioning 12 instances (gpu-nv4). expected ready ~7m. current inflight: provisioning.
sam: note: autoscaler was suppressed earlier because org quota for preemptible GPUs hit; we've requested quota bump but not approved yet. this is why fallback kicked in instead of scale earlier.
anjali: open action: follow up with capacity planning to increase baseline for EU. filing a ticket now.
maria: I'll also add a temporary rule to prefer hosted for low-priority routes to reduce future noise: adding `overflow_threshold: 0.80` and `prefer_hosted_for: [priority=low, env=staging]`
(quoted config)
```
route_overflow:
  primary: dedicated-eu-central
  fallback: hosted-eu
  overflow_threshold: 0.80
  prefer_hosted_for:
    - priority=low
    - env=staging
```
liam: scaling completed, 12 nodes up. gpu mem pressure easing to ~82% in the pool. queued reqs down to 90.
capacity-bot: [RESOLVED] pool=dedicated-eu-central mem_util=81.6% queued_reqs=88 at 2026-03-18T15:33:20Z
nora: thanks — can we get a quick incident blurb for CS and a short RCA pointer?
maria: yes. short blurb: unexpected internal batch canary routed to dedicated, autoscaler suppressed by quota, automatic fallback to hosted prevented SLA breaches, temporary scale and routing changes restored headroom. follow-up: quota bump, routing rule changes, and update default routing for canaries.
sam: i'll capture logs and timeline into the incident doc. assigning follow-ups: quota request (liam), routing rule PR (maria), datapipe canary runbook update (anjali).
liam: will open quota request with infra-ops and cc procurement.
anjali: datapipe team will pause canaries by default for 24h and add a traffic tag.
maria: excellent. closing thread once incident doc is linked. thanks all. :thumbsup:
